newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cockerill sells stake in troubled plant.
newsitem.headline: Cockerill sells stake in troubled plant.

text.p: Belgium's largest steel maker Cockerill Sambre said on Tuesday it was selling its 32 percent stake in steel products company Laminoirs de Longtain to Laminoirs' majority shareholder Boel Invest.
The sale was for a symbolic one franc, reflecting the cash difficulties Laminoirs suffered in recent years, Cockerill spokesman Christophe Weerts, told Reuters.
Boel Invest is part of privately-owned Belgian steel group Usines Gustave Boel, which recently formed an alliance with Dutch Hoogovens.
In view of Laminoirs order book there would be work for the company's 225 staff until the end of September. Boel Invest had not ruled out finding another partner for Laminoir.

Cockerill, which booked a nine billion franc loss in 1996, is working on a restructuring plan to curb costs and crank up competitiveness. It aims to cut its workforce by 2,135 to 7,777 by the year 2000 as part of its Horizon 2000 plan.
